unit.why: A single anecdote, heard from the narrator's master, about the pre-Hasidic gaon R. Heschel and the rebuker he kept: the rebuker held back his reproach because he saw the Tosafists accompanying him.

stories.start_quote: פ״א שמעתי ממנו ז״ל בי הגאון
stories.summary_en: R. Heschel kept a righteous man as a permanent rebuker. One morning he was late to prayer because he was absorbed in a Tosafot passage. The rebuker had stood ready to scold him but kept silent, explaining afterwards that he had seen the Ri and Rabbenu Tam enter with him.

tags.why: praises the pre-Hasidic gaon R. Heschel, whose study draws the Tosafists to him

quotes: היה לו עיון גדול באיזה דיבור תוס׳
tags.why: his intense Talmud study causes the delay

quotes: מלכנוס לבית הכנסת להתפלל בזמנו כדרכו תמיד
tags.why: his lateness to communal prayer is the issue

quotes: ראיתי אשר עם ביאתך באו עמך הר"י והר״ת
tags.why: the rebuker sees what others cannot

quotes: ראיתי אשר עם ביאתך באו עמך הר"י והר״ת
tags.why: a waking vision of the souls of the Tosafists

quotes: באו עמך הר"י והר״ת בעל התוס׳
tags.why: the souls of departed sages are present, though no one speaks with them

quotes: איך הייתי יכול להעיז ולפתוח פי נגד עיניהם
tags.why: the rebuker is held back by reverence for the sages

quotes: על מה ולמה לא הוכחת אותי כלל
tags.why: the gaon learns afterwards the hidden reason for the silence
framed as told by the narrator's master
the gaon's humility in keeping a rebuker, and the merit of his study
